lessons.title: Why a maintained knowledge base matters
lessons.subtitle: Traceable knowledge retrieval for one person

sections.title: The documentation paradox
sections.content:
"We discussed this. I just cannot find the decision." A record is missing here: the search costs time, and the decision waits.

A CRM or a decision log holds the decision, owners and sources. Interpreting, settling conflicts and approving stay with you.

sections.title: BI for one person
sections.content:
A BI system answers a controller's defined questions from maintained data. Your notes sit in several places, and you search by hand. An Obsidian vault with Smart Connections or Copilot does that search for one person.

You ask: "Which decisions about Customer Y are documented in the last 90 days?" The answer must carry source paths, and you check them before you believe it.

More notes help only when maintenance, metadata, provenance and retrieval quality are right.

quiz.questionText: Which capability can AI-assisted search add to a knowledge base?
quiz.explanation: Embeddings find notes that match in meaning, even without the same words. Quality, cost and data flow depend on model, index and configuration.

lessons.title: Setup walkthrough (bonus)
lessons.subtitle: Set up Obsidian and five core plugins

sections.title: Installing Obsidian
sections.content:
This lesson has no time limit.

**Step 1:** Download the current build for your operating system from `obsidian.md`, verify the source and install it.

**Step 2: decide on synchronization.** Data can leave the device even from a local vault. Before any sync service, check encryption, accounts, device access, recovery and your organization's approval.

**Step 3: import the vault template.**

Option A: Create an empty practice vault, unzip `vault-template.zip` and copy its contents into it.

Option B: Back up an existing vault and copy only the directories you need. Overwrite no file without a diff and a backup.

sections.title: The 5 core plugins
sections.content:
A community plugin is someone else's code with access to your vault. Check the publisher, repository, version, change history, permissions, data flow and maintenance first. Enable only what the exercise needs, and record version, permissions and how to roll it back.

**Course configuration:**
1. **Templater:** template folder `_System/Templates`, JavaScript only for a reviewed need
2. **Dataview:** JavaScript queries only after a code review
3. **Smart Connections:** verify the embedding model and network access
4. **Obsidian Copilot:** verify provider, model, billing, retention and API-key storage
5. **Note Companion:** optional, automatic moves off

Test every plugin with fictional data. For models, prices and menus, current documentation applies.

sections.title: Web Clipper + your first daily note
sections.content:
**Obsidian Web Clipper in the browser:**
1. Install the extension via the official Clipper page from the browser's official source.
2. Select the practice vault and `00 Inbox/` as the target.
3. Leave the AI Interpreter off for now. It sends content to a model provider.

Test with a non-sensitive public page and check the title, URL, capture date and content of the new note.

**First daily note:**
Cmd/Ctrl+P → `Templater: insert template` → `_System/Templates/daily-note.md`.

Then verify:
- plugins and versions as expected
- Clipper writes to the practice folder
- template produces file name and fields
- chat features use only the documented configuration

If a check fails, stop there, fix the error and only then use real data.

scenarios.question: Note: proposal draft for a new customer, due this coming Friday.

options.label: Projects: has a clear deadline
options.explanation: A deadline means Project. After the decision the note goes to Archive.

options.label: Areas: sales is ongoing
options.explanation: Sales in general is an Area; this proposal has a deadline.

options.label: Resources: look up proposal templates
options.explanation: That fits the template; this proposal is a Project.

options.label: Archive: after submission
options.explanation: Only after submission. Today it is an active Project.

options.label: Projects: you do have annual reviews
options.explanation: Each review is a Project; the framework you reuse.

options.explanation: Only if you keep developing it. Otherwise it is a Resource.

options.label: Resources: reference material for recurring tasks

options.label: Archive: it mattered in April
options.explanation: You need it every week, so it does not belong in Archive.

options.label: Resources: to prepare for the next negotiation
options.explanation: Resources are templates. Link the single case from the next negotiation.

options.label: Archive: closed, but findable
options.explanation: Closed means Archive. Search and Copilot still find the note.

sections.title: PARA as a four-part storage structure
sections.content:
PARA = **Projects, Areas, Resources, Archive.**

- **Projects:** anything with an endpoint, such as the fictitious project "Close the proposal for Customer Alpha"
- **Areas:** ongoing responsibilities with no endpoint, such as sales, finance or team
- **Resources:** reference material like articles, PDFs and templates
- **Archive:** completed projects and inactive resources

Where findability, retention or data protection require something else, they take priority over PARA.

sections.title: The skeleton in the vault
sections.content:
```
vault-root/
├── 00 Inbox/              ← new input
├── 10 Projects/
│   └── Projekt-Angebot-Mueller/
│       └── _MOC.md       ← overview note
├── 20 Areas/
│   ├── Vertrieb/
│   ├── Finanzen/
│   ├── Team/
│   └── Strategie/
├── 30 Resources/
│   ├── Branche/
│   ├── KI-Tools/
│   └── Vorlagen/
├── 40 Archive/
├── 50 Daily/
└── _System/
    ├── Templates/
    └── Dashboards/
```

The German folder names come from the supplied template. If you imported it in Lesson 3.0, the structure is already there.

**Bounded migration exercise:**
1. Check the inbox
2. Move in three to five active Projects
3. Create only the Areas you need now
4. File a small, representative set of references
5. Move completed material to Archive

Everything else waits until search, links and backup work on this sample.

sections.title: MOC: the master-note concept
sections.content:
**MOC = Map of Content.** One master note per project serves as the status hub for everything else.

Fictitious structure from `10 Projects/Projekt-Kunde-Alpha/_MOC.md`:

```markdown
---
status: aktiv
projekt: Kunde-Alpha-Fiktivfall
---

# Proposal for Customer Alpha (fictitious)

## Goal
Draft for three fictitious sample machines; price and delivery date are unverified placeholders.

## Status
- [x] fictitious inquiry recorded
- [ ] verify technical details
- [ ] approve the proposal internally

## Participants
- Fictitious role Alpha: decision
- Fictitious role Beta: price approval

## Open questions
- Have price, availability and discount been confirmed?
```

The YAML fields keep the template's German identifiers. A real MOC carries only necessary, approved data with matching access rights.

sections.title: Tagging policy
sections.content:
Start with a small, documented tag set, for example:
- `#todo`: open action
- `#entscheidung`: documented decision
- `#warten-auf`: blocked action
- `#idee`: untested proposal
- `#followup`: item to review again
- `#archivieren`: archive candidate

Use folders for coarse filing, MOCs for Project context and tags for the few states that cut across everything. Personal names and sensitive attributes go into no tag without a data policy.

Ten tags is a starting limit. If the set grows, check overlaps, write down meanings and test whether your queries still answer predictably.

quiz.explanation: PARA comes from Tiago Forte: Projects have a clear end, Areas keep running, Resources serve as reference, Archive holds what is done.

answerOptions.text: Map of Content: one master note per project as status hub

quiz.explanation: One maintained overview note gathers a Project's goal, status, next action, participants and links.

sections.title: Smart Connections in action
sections.content:
You create a new, fictitious note: volume discount for Customer Alpha, yes or no? Smart Connections suggests older discount notes and a current policy.

A similarity score proves nothing. Whether the current approval rule still allows these terms shows only in the source note, with date and context.

Smart Connections works with embeddings, vectors for semantic similarity. Model, where it runs, network access and cost are in your plugin configuration.

sections.title: Copilot as a vault search interface
sections.content:
In the isolated practice vault you ask Copilot: "Which fictitious discount decisions are documented in the last 90 days? Give the file path and date for each statement."

You get a search draft back, say on Customer Alpha, Beta and Gamma. Open every linked note, check the context and look for gaps and contradictions.

Second practice question: "Summarize the approved practice notes on Customer Alpha and flag every statement without a source."

Copilot guarantees neither speed nor accuracy. Source links make the result checkable; the checking is yours.

sections.title: Asking the right questions
sections.content:
Copilot answers as well as your question and index allow. Three rules help:

**Concrete:** "Which discount decisions are documented in the last 90 days?" instead of "What do I think about pricing policy?"

**Time-bound:** a period such as "Q1 2026" or "since March 2026", when it fits the task.

**Source-linked:** for every statement the file path, date and passage.

Measure retrieval time, missing-source rate and correction effort against your old workflow. If the numbers do not improve, switch the configuration off again.

quiz.questionText: How does Smart Connections work technically?

answerOptions.text: Embeddings: notes as vectors, compared by meaning
GraphRAG with an external vector store

quiz.explanation: Smart Connections compares meaning, not keywords. Which model computes the vectors, and where your note content goes, is in your current configuration.

quiz.questionText: Three principles of good Copilot questions?
quiz.explanation: That narrows the hits and makes them checkable. It still does not guarantee accuracy.

lessons.title: Obsidian Web Clipper
lessons.subtitle: From browser content to a reviewed vault note

props.title: Remove PII from a clipping before it goes into the vault
props.scenario: All details are invented dummy data. Still mark every token a real clipping must not store permanently: names, email, phone, internal revenue and customer data.
props.text: A fictitious person posted on LinkedIn yesterday: our fictitious company Fiktivwerk GmbH made 2.4 million euros in Q1 revenue, the sales lead Fictitious Contact reported a deal with Customer Beta worth 450000 euros. Contact at Fiktivwerk: demo.person@example.invalid or +49-000-000000-DUMMY. The analysis: we should also talk to Customer Gamma in Q2.

sections.title: The browser-tab reality
sections.content:
Count your open tabs, the ones for reading later and the ones kept as reference. A tab has no fixed location, no metadata and no way back.

The workflow: Web Clipper saves the article, the AI Interpreter proposes metadata, Obsidian indexes the note. You time each article yourself.

sections.title: Review a clip with the AI Interpreter
sections.content:
Take a non-sensitive public article and start Web Clipper. The panel offers title, target folder, tags, template and an optional summary.

Before saving, verify:
- title, canonical URL and capture date
- the target folder against the storage rule
- tags against the documented tag set
- every summary statement against the article
- that embedded personal or confidential details are removed

With the AI Interpreter active, the article goes to the configured model provider. So check provider, model, API-key storage, retention and cost, and store every summary with its source.

sections.title: A capture criterion
sections.content:
Save an article when it touches an active Project, supplies reference material you use regularly, or is a documented source that is hard to replace. Duplicates, articles with no foreseeable use and unsupported claims stay out.

The test before saving: "I will use this source for [Project or Area] to answer [specific question]." If that sentence does not hold, close the tab.

**Exercise:** Take no more than three open tabs. Store source, capture date and intended use, review the generated fields and process the notes in the next scheduled inbox session.

quiz.questionText: What does the AI Interpreter do in Web Clipper?

answerOptions.text: Summarizes, tags and suggests a folder before import

quiz.explanation: It proposes a summary, tags and a folder before import. Which provider sees the content to do that is in your configuration.

lessons.title: Daily workflow and precise prompts
lessons.subtitle: Inbox maintenance with RCTFC and reviewable output

props.title: Which daily Obsidian prompt is reviewable?
props.scenario: You want to summarize last work week from the practice vault for the weekly report. Which prompt sets sources, format and boundaries?

candidates.label: Variant A: the blanket ask
candidates.critique: Role, time frame and format are missing. Copilot guesses and often returns generic bullets or, lacking context, a refusal.

candidates.label: Variant B: structured, but open-ended
candidates.prompt: Based on the daily notes from the last 7 days: summarize the key decisions and blockers for the weekly report.
candidates.critique: Time frame, source and goal are there. Without a format (structure, word limit) and a role (for whom?), results vary a lot.

candidates.label: Variant C: RCTFC + structured output
candidates.prompt:
Role: Chief of Staff, writing for management.
Context: daily notes from 2026-04-14 to 2026-04-20 in the vault.
Task: create a weekly report.
Format: Markdown, 3 sections (1. Highlights, 3 bullet points, max 15 words each; 2. Blockers with a proposed solution, max 3; 3. Next week, max 5 lines).
Off-limits: adverbs like "successful", "productive", "focused".
Source: facts from the notes only, no additions or opinions.
Constraint: if the time frame has no data, say so and make nothing up.
candidates.critique: The brief sets RCTFC fields, an output schema, banned wording and a source rule. That makes repeated outputs comparable and reviewable.

sections.title: A bounded maintenance workflow
sections.content:
Without maintenance a knowledge base turns back into a pile of files. A fixed, bounded session in four steps prevents that:

1. **Inspect the inbox:** count new entries; never forward real data automatically without approval.
2. **Classify:** assign each entry to Project, Area, Resource or Archive; unclear entries stay flagged in the inbox.
3. **Update MOCs:** add status, next action and source link for the affected Projects.
4. **Create the daily note:** carry priorities and open points over from reviewed records.

The time box follows your volume. Record backlog and misclassification, because an empty inbox proves nothing when entries sit in the wrong place.

sections.title: RCTFC: the prompt schema
sections.content:
**RCTFC** means **Role, Context, Task, Format, Constraints.**

Open request:
> "Write a customer decline email."

Structured brief:
- **Role:** sales representative at a mid-sized mechanical-engineering company
- **Context:** fictional established Customer Alpha; a documented request cannot be fulfilled
- **Task:** prepare an internal decline-email draft
- **Format:** subject, greeting, two paragraphs, signature
- **Constraints:** fewer than 120 words, no invented reasons or commitments, any alternative only as a reviewed placeholder

Every field takes a decision off the model that it would otherwise guess. You still review the draft. The template is `P020-rctfc-template` in the course materials.

sections.title: Structured Output (JSON) + Few-shot + CoT
sections.content:
**Structured output (JSON):** When a machine processes the answer further, it needs a fixed schema and technical validation.

```
Analyze this fictitious meeting transcript. Return strictly valid JSON:
{
  "entscheidungen": [{"text": "...", "verantwortlich": null}],
  "action_items": [{"text": "...", "fälligkeit": null, "verantwortlich": null}],
  "offene_fragen": [{"text": "...", "wer_antwortet": null}]
}
Use null for unknown values. Do not invent details.
```

Later workflow steps may depend on the German keys, so they stay. Validate the result against the schema before n8n or Python use it; invalid JSON goes to a documented error path.

**Few-shot:** Two or three representative examples show the model the pattern, but they prove no accuracy.

**Reviewable intermediate results (CoT):** For complex tasks, ask for short evidence and assumptions. Do not ask for hidden reasoning, and skip intermediate steps on simple text tasks.

Whether routine, schema or examples pay off, you measure on the task at hand.

quiz.explanation: Each of the five fields takes a decision off the model that it would otherwise guess from general patterns.

quiz.questionText: Which request is appropriate for a complex analysis?

answerOptions.text: Request complete hidden reasoning for every task
Ask for short, reviewable evidence and assumptions
Review it only through an API and never through a user interface
Tie the method to one fixed model name

quiz.explanation: Evidence and assumptions make the analysis checkable. You do not need hidden reasoning for that, and it proves nothing about quality.

sections.title: The third connection
sections.content:
You know two ways into the vault: the plugin inside Obsidian, and copy and paste. The third is MCP, a programmatic interface. It lets Claude do more, so you review more.

The course reference `obsidian-claude-code-mcp` describes a WebSocket bridge. Before using it, review the repository, version, maintainer, license, dependencies, security notices and compatibility.

Depending on its tools, the server reads, searches, creates or modifies notes. Start on a copy of the practice vault, read-only and with one folder.

sections.title: Setup
sections.content:
The course bundle contains `install-obsidian-claude-code-mcp.sh`. Read every setup script before you run it.

**Before execution:**
1. Read the script and pinned dependency versions
2. Verify the repository URL and commit
3. Back up the Claude Code configuration
4. Set an explicit path to a copied practice vault
5. Review loopback binding, port and authentication for the bridge
6. Confirm that existing MCP entries are not overwritten
7. Do not provide secrets as command arguments

Then test start and stop, and record changed files, running processes and the complete rollback.

sections.title: The first query
sections.content:
The first test is read-only, in the copied practice vault:

> "List the top-level directories and count Markdown files in each. Do not open file contents and do not perform any write action."

Compare the output with a local file listing. If an unapproved directory shows up, the test failed.

Then a bounded task:
> "Read only approved MOCs in `10 Projects/` with `status: aktiv`. Prepare an internal status draft with source path and date for every statement. Do not write a file yet."

Claude may write only after sources, permissions and output are reviewed, and then only to a separate output directory. You measure runtime and correction effort yourself.

sections.title: More use cases
sections.content:
**Follow-up extraction:**
> "Find all open `#warten-auf` entries in the approved practice notes. Create internal drafts and name the source file for each statement. Don't send anything."

**Decision overview:**
> "List practice notes tagged `#entscheidung`. Give the date, topic, decision, follow-up action and source file for each. Flag any contradictions."

**Fictitious customer profile:**
> "Build a profile for Customer Alpha (fictitious) from the approved practice notes. Don't use any real personal or contact data."

MCP does not make your notes more correct. Permissions, data minimization, source review and read-only tests stay, and for roadmaps and integrations the current official documentation applies.

quiz.questionText: What does MCP do differently than Copilot for Obsidian?

answerOptions.text: MCP exposes tools; Copilot is an interface inside Obsidian
MCP uses GPT-4, Copilot uses Claude

quiz.explanation: MCP is a tool interface for compatible clients. Transport and available actions depend on the specific server.
